title: How Sam Parr launched Hampton, a founder peer network, to ~$1M ARR with no website
summary: Sam Parr explains how he and co-founder Joe Spiser tested demand with a public tweet, personally called every respondent, and sold group spots through a Stripe link before building anything. He covers co-founder alignment, designing groups around fast vulnerability, selective admissions, and why hiring a CEO too early backfired.

principles.text: Validate demand by publicly posting a generic offer and counting replies. If one audience doesn't respond, switch audiences.
principles.quote: And I got like another 300 replies. And I started calling them and they were like, "Take my money. I'm in."

principles.text: Skip the website and polish at the start. Personally interview every lead and take payment through a simple link.
principles.quote: I had the 300 people on that list. I called all of them and I interviewed 100% of them and at the end of the interview it was like Joe I think this person wants in.

principles.text: Before partnering, each person writes answers to the same questions separately (goals, limits, values), then compare them.
principles.quote: I put it in a document and I go, "Copy this document and you go write your answers. I'll go write my answers."

principles.text: Design community experiences for speed to vulnerability. Candid, confrontational-with-love conversations create the value.
principles.quote: it's speed to vulnerability. I think that's like the key is how do I make someone break really fast?

principles.text: Don't grow for growth's sake. Curate who gets in and be willing to turn away money to protect the product.
principles.quote: you can't grow for growth's sake. I can't just throw people into this. That will ruin it.

principles.text: Don't hire a CEO to hand off a problem you're intimidated by. Handing off out of fear is abdication, not delegation.
principles.quote: I also think I was intimidated a little bit by the opportunity and how to pull it off. And so I wanted to hand that off to someone which is uh not a good reason probably to hire someone.
